top_choice_rationale: P001 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn, B001) is a measurement advance with a jointly authored core (Berry 1994; BLP 1995). It made substitution patterns, markups and welfare counterfactuals recoverable from market data when prices are endogenous, which earlier reduced-form work could not do. It has about three decades of use in merger review, antitrust and regulation, and it has spread into trade, productivity and markup measurement. Its maturity is not contested, and the credit can be drawn cleanly with a method-level citation. The main costs remain toolkit versus discovery, the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, and the documented sensitivity of applied estimates to numerics, instruments and functional form. I judge these costs smaller than the cost of making no award. My assessment of the sensitivities rests on background knowledge and I have not independently verified adoption or citation claims. P000 is ranked second because the slate has no other substantive option, and a mature, well-attributed achievement should not be passed over.
recusal_note: No tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is apparent from the profile. Per Krusell (secretary) is a frequent co-author and John Hassler (chair) a co-author, and I am an IIES colleague of both. Both also support P001, so their agreement is not independent evidence of merit. My research on firm dynamics, misallocation and creative destruction, and my long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow and others, is topically adjacent to the demand and markup tools but involves no credited name. I disclose this and do not adjudicate it.
